quests.instruction: It is a chilly morning, so Priya puts a warm jumper over her head and onto her body. What does she do with the jumper?
quests.hint: The jumper stays on her body all day.
quests.explanation: Wear means to have clothes or shoes on your body. We wear a jumper, a hat or shoes.
quests.funFact: Many school uniforms are worn so that all children in the school look alike.

quests.instruction: Ravi pulls the little tab up the front of his coat until the two sides join. What is he doing?
quests.hint: A metal or plastic tab slides along teeth.
quests.explanation: Zip means to close something by sliding a zipper. Zip a coat, a bag or a pencil case.
quests.funFact: The zipper was first used on boots and tobacco pouches before it reached clothes.

quests.instruction: Sara makes a loop with her shoelaces and pulls them into a bow. Choose the action word that matches.
quests.hint: Two ends of a string are joined in a knot.
quests.explanation: Tie means to join two ends of a string, rope or lace in a knot or bow.
quests.funFact: A bow is a simple knot that is easy to undo by pulling one end.

quests.instruction: Dev smooths his tangled hair with a tool that has a row of teeth. What is he doing?
quests.hint: The tool he uses has teeth in a row.
quests.explanation: Comb means to tidy hair with a comb, a tool with a row of teeth.
quests.funFact: The comb is one of the oldest grooming tools still used today.

quests.instruction: After her swim, Zoe rubs a towel over her wet hair. Which verb describes the action?
quests.hint: Water goes from her hair into the towel.
quests.explanation: Dry means to take the water off something or to let it go away.
quests.funFact: Hair dries faster in a warm, windy place than in a cool, still one.

quests.instruction: Leo has put shampoo in his hair and now lets clean water run over it. What does he do?
quests.hint: The soap has to leave his hair.
quests.explanation: Rinse means to wash soap away with clean water.
quests.funFact: Rinse is also the last step when you wash fruit before eating it.

quests.instruction: Mia puts a piece of toast in her mouth and moves her teeth up and down. Which action word is being shown?
quests.hint: The food stays in her mouth and gets smaller.
quests.explanation: Chew means to crush food with your teeth before swallowing it.
quests.funFact: Chewing mixes food with saliva, which starts breaking it down.

quests.instruction: When the carrot is soft in Noor's mouth, she sends it down her throat. What does she do?
quests.hint: Food leaves her mouth and goes toward her stomach.
quests.explanation: Swallow means to move food or drink from your mouth down your throat.
quests.funFact: Muscles in your throat push food down, so swallowing does not depend on gravity alone.

quests.instruction: Max opens his mouth wide and cuts through the sandwich with his front teeth. Choose the best verb.
quests.hint: His front teeth make the first cut.
quests.explanation: Bite means to cut or hold something with your teeth.
quests.funFact: The word 'bite' also describes a small piece of food: 'Take one more bite.'

quests.instruction: The glass is empty, so Mum puts water into it until it is nearly full. What does she do?
quests.hint: The water level goes up.
quests.explanation: Fill means to put in something until there is no more room for it.
quests.funFact: A full glass is easier to spill, so people often fill it only to the middle.

quests.instruction: Tom bumps the table, and juice runs out of his cup onto the floor. Which verb matches what happens?
quests.hint: It was not supposed to come out.
quests.explanation: Spill means to let a liquid flow out by accident. Pour is when you do it on purpose.
quests.funFact: There is an English saying: 'Don't cry over spilled milk.'

quests.instruction: After drinking all the juice, Ella turns the jug upside down. She wants to ___ it before washing.
quests.hint: Nothing should be left inside.
quests.explanation: Empty means to take everything out of a container so nothing is left.
quests.funFact: Empty is also an adjective: an empty jug has nothing in it.

quests.instruction: Grandpa uses a knife to make thin pieces of bread from the loaf. What is he doing?
quests.hint: The loaf becomes several flat pieces.
quests.explanation: Slice means to cut something into thin, flat pieces.
quests.funFact: A slice of bread is flat, while a chunk of bread is a thick, uneven piece.

quests.instruction: Hana pulls the skin off a banana before eating it. Which verb fits the scene?
quests.hint: The outside layer comes off.
quests.explanation: Peel means to take the skin or outer layer off a fruit or vegetable.
quests.funFact: You can also peel paint or a sticker.

quests.instruction: Jay puts flour, eggs and milk in a bowl and turns them together with a spoon. What is he doing?
quests.hint: Many things become one.
quests.explanation: Mix means to put different things together so they become one.
quests.funFact: If you mix yellow and blue paint, you get green.

quests.instruction: At a school party, Dad puts a plate of rice in front of each child. Choose the action word that matches.
quests.hint: Food goes from the kitchen to the table.
quests.explanation: Serve means to give food or drink to people at a table.
quests.funFact: The person who serves food in a restaurant is called a server.

quests.instruction: Aisha uses a knife to put a thin layer of butter on her bread. What does she do?
quests.hint: The butter goes out over the whole slice.
quests.explanation: Spread means to cover a surface with a thin layer of something.
quests.funFact: News and colds can spread from person to person, just like butter spreads on bread.

quests.instruction: Before adding more salt, Ben puts a little soup on a spoon and tries it. Which verb describes the action?
quests.hint: He finds out what the soup is like by trying it.
quests.explanation: Taste means to try a small bit of food to find out what it is like.
quests.funFact: Your tongue can tell sweet, salty, sour and bitter tastes.

quests.instruction: Meena makes her T-shirt flat and puts one side over the other, and the shirt becomes small and neat. What does she do?
quests.hint: The shirt becomes a small square.
quests.explanation: Fold means to bend something so one part lies over another part.
quests.funFact: Paper can be folded into a boat, a plane or a crane.

quests.instruction: Dad puts the wet shirt over a line outside, using a peg to hold it. Which action word is being shown?
quests.hint: The shirt is up in the air and is not lying down.
quests.explanation: Hang means to fix something at the top so that the rest of it falls down.
quests.funFact: Clothes hung in sunshine can dry faster.

quests.instruction: Before the trip, Rina puts her clothes and a toothbrush into a suitcase. What is she doing?
quests.hint: Things go into a bag for later.
quests.explanation: Pack means to put things into a bag or box so you can take them somewhere.
quests.funFact: Rolling clothes can help fit more into a suitcase.

quests.instruction: Before leaving home, Mum uses a key so nobody can come in. Choose the best verb.
quests.hint: Nobody can open it without the key.
quests.explanation: Lock means to close something with a key so that it cannot be opened easily.
quests.funFact: Some modern locks open with a code or a fingerprint instead of a key.

quests.instruction: To call the lift, Omar puts his finger on the button and pushes in. What does he do?
quests.hint: A button goes in.
quests.explanation: Press means to push something down or in with your finger or hand.
quests.funFact: Press is also what you do to a flower to keep it flat in a book.

quests.instruction: Nina moves a small lever to make the light go on. Which verb matches what happens?
quests.hint: It has two positions, on and off.
quests.explanation: Switch means to change something from one state to another, like on to off.
quests.funFact: Some lights need two switches, one at each end of a corridor.

quests.instruction: The baby cannot hold a spoon yet, so Dad puts the food in her mouth for her. What does he do?
quests.hint: She needs help to eat.
quests.explanation: Feed means to give food to a person or an animal that cannot eat alone.
quests.funFact: Baby birds open their mouths wide so their parents can feed them.

quests.instruction: It is bath time, and Mum washes the baby with warm water in a small tub. Which verb fits the scene?
quests.hint: The baby gets clean in water.
quests.explanation: Bathe means to wash someone or yourself by sitting in or being in water.
quests.funFact: Babies are bathed in warm, not hot, water.

quests.instruction: The baby is crying, so Anu holds her and moves gently from side to side until she calms down. What does she do?
quests.hint: Slow and gentle movements make a baby feel safe.
quests.explanation: Rock means to move slowly from side to side or back and forth, often to calm a baby.
quests.funFact: A rocking chair is named after this slow backward and forward movement.

quests.instruction: Tara holds a rope in both hands and swings it over her head and under her feet as she hops. Choose the action word that matches.
quests.hint: She uses a rope, and she jumps it.
quests.explanation: Skip means to jump lightly over a rope, or move with a hop on each foot.
quests.funFact: Skipping rope is a good way for children to build strong legs.

quests.instruction: Zoe stands in the middle of the garden with her arms out and turns round and round. What is she doing?
quests.hint: She stays in one place while she turns.
quests.explanation: Spin means to turn round and round quickly, usually staying in the same place.
quests.funFact: A top spins because turning things like to keep turning in the same direction.

quests.instruction: The rubber ball hits the floor and goes back up again. Which verb describes the action?
quests.hint: It rises again after it touches the floor.
quests.explanation: Bounce means to hit a surface and go back up. Rubber balls bounce.
quests.funFact: A bouncy ball is full of rubber that springs back to its shape after it is squashed.
